STEP 1 - Scene: This is a buffet-style plate holding a fried chicken sandwich, two pieces of fried chicken nugget or popcorn chicken, a piece of baked fish (or similar fish/meat), a beef patty or meat slice, and two pieces of California roll sushi.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white dinner plate, about 27 cm across. Area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Chicken sandwich (bun plus fried chicken patty)
- Fried chicken pieces (2)
- Baked fish piece (skin on)
- Breaded or ground beef slice
- California roll pieces (2)

STEP 4 - Area (food covers about 46% of the plate):

| Item | Share of plate | Area |
|---|---|---|
| Sandwich | 20% | 114 cm² |
| Fried chicken pieces | 6% | 34 cm² |
| Fish | 10% | 57 cm² |
| Beef slice | 5% | 29 cm² |
| Sushi pieces | 5% | 29 cm² |
| **Total** | **46%** | |

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Sandwich: 114 cm² × 5 cm = 570 ml
- Fried chicken: 34 cm² × 3 cm = 102 ml
- Fish: 57 cm² × 2 cm = 114 ml
- Beef: 29 cm² × 1.5 cm = 44 ml
- Sushi: 29 cm² × 2.5 cm = 73 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Sandwich: the bun is airy, so I used a mixed density of 0.35, giving about 200 g.
- Fried chicken: 102 ml × 0.6 (irregular, gappy shapes) ≈ 60 g.
- Fish: 114 ml × 0.7 (it includes bones and skin) ≈ 80 g.
- Beef: 44 ml × 0.9 ≈ 40 g.
- Sushi: 73 ml × 0.9 ≈ 65 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Sandwich: 200 g × 270 kcal/100 g = 540 kcal
- Fried chicken: 60 g × 280 kcal/100 g = 168 kcal
- Fish: 80 g × 170 kcal/100 g = 136 kcal
- Beef: 40 g × 250 kcal/100 g = 100 kcal
- Sushi: 65 g × 150 kcal/100 g = 98 kcal

**Total: about 445 g and 1,042 kcal.**

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The plate holds a full fried chicken sandwich plus several sides, so a total of about 1,000 kcal is plausible.
